content.value_statement: Building Git-compatible repository services requires careful object, pack, and ref handling. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical Rust patterns for gitoxide-based operations.
actual_capabilities: Explains key gitoxide crates for objects, hashes, packs, and transport.
Shows Rust patterns for opening or creating bare repositories.
Demonstrates object reads, blob writes, commit construction, and reference updates.
Outlines Smart HTTP upload-pack and receive-pack route handlers.
Shows packfile generation from want and have object sets.
Describes a Guts commit extension with signature verification metadata.
limitations: Provides illustrative Rust snippets, not a complete runnable service.
Mentions permission checks but does not define a full authorization policy.
Targets gitoxide and Guts-style repositories, so other Git libraries need adaptation.
Does not cover shallow clone, partial clone, or recovery behavior in depth.

use_cases.title: Prototype Git Services
use_cases.description: Use the patterns to sketch upload-pack, receive-pack, object storage, and ref update flows.

use_cases.title: Review Repository Designs
use_cases.description: Compare a planned Git-compatible service against the object, commit, packfile, and reference concepts shown here.

use_cases.title: Extend Guts Integrations
use_cases.description: Adapt the Guts commit metadata pattern for signed commits and consensus-related repository features.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Building Blocks
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the gitoxide crates named in this skill and how they relate to Git objects, hashes, packs, and transport.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Repository Operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this skill, outline the steps for opening a bare repository, reading objects, writing blobs, and creating commits.

prompt_templates.title: Design Smart HTTP Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design an upload-pack and receive-pack flow with parsing, permission checks, packfile handling, and response types.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Git Service Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my gitoxide-based service design against this skill and identify missing validation, authorization, reference safety, and packfile handling steps.

output_examples.input: Design a receive-pack flow for a Rust Git service.
output: Parse commands and pack data from the request body.
Verify push permissions before accepting repository mutations.
Apply the packfile, then update each reference with atomic checks.
Return a Git receive-pack response with a clear success or error result.

output_examples.output: The skill shows listing references, updating references with expected old values, creating new references, and reading HEAD from the repository.

output_examples.input: Explain how Guts extends Git commits.
output_examples.output: A Guts commit wraps a standard Git commit with an Ed25519 signature, signer public key, and optional consensus round metadata.

best_practices: Validate Git object identifiers and request bodies before repository access.
Check write permissions before applying packfiles or updating references.
Use atomic reference updates when old object IDs are available.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the snippets as complete production code without missing service controls.
Do not update references without checking expected old values when concurrency matters.
Do not accept arbitrary pack data without size limits, validation, and permission checks.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design Git-compatible repository operations in Rust using gitoxide and Guts-oriented patterns.

faq.question: Does it provide a complete Git server?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation patterns and examples, but service wiring and production controls remain your responsibility.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: The skill describes Smart HTTP server handlers, but the skill file itself does not make network requests.

faq.question: What Rust library does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on gitoxide, including gix, gix-object, gix-hash, gix-pack, and gix-transport concepts.

faq.question: Is the sample code production-ready?
faq.answer: No. Treat it as a starting point and add validation, authorization, limits, tests, and error handling.
